differences.what: In B the side face of carton 6's dark-brown base band picks up a mirror-grey floor reflection (RGB 93/90/86 against A's 15/10/6), so the band's colour block breaks between front and side and the base reads like glass or chrome. A keeps the band solid dark brown.
In B the side of the green carton's base band is washed to a grey-green by a translucent diagonal sheen across the seam, so the base looks like an acrylic sleeve rather than a printed band.
The side faces of the red, blue and light-blue base bands in B carry hard-edged diagonal light triangles that read as a glassy plinth. In A these faces are clean, solid colour with a soft falloff.
On the cream gable the tweeter waveguide nearly disappears in B (luminance range 55 against 93 in A). A shows the scoop's rim highlight and shading clearly.
The light-blue gable's waveguide is softer and less defined in B (range 67 against 83).
A grounds the cartons better: in front of the cream carton A's floor drops to 46 against 55 on the open floor, while B's is 72 against 70.
B has a faint blurred glow on the floor below the white earmilk logos on the green and dark cartons.
B's backdrop is brighter and more even (about 115 at both top corners against A's 71 and 93), giving the dark-brown gable more separation and a more open feel.
A's foreground floor sinks to about 39 luma, a heavy, murky band under the lineup; B's sits at about 57.
